title: Richard III: Good Guy or Evil Putz?
summary: Hosts examine whether Richard III was the villainous hunchback of Shakespeare's play or a misrepresented king. They cover the Wars of the Roses and the York-Lancaster struggle, Richard's rise after Edward IV's death, the disappearance of the Princes in the Tower, the Tudor smear campaign and Thomas More's account, the Ricardian movement, Josephine Tey's novel The Daughter of Time, Philippa Langley's search that located his remains under a Leicester car park in 2012, DNA confirmation, and his reinterment at Leicester Cathedral. Ends with a listener mail segment about an Eagle Scout.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the episode on whether Richard III was a lousy king or a misrepresented one.

segments.title: Shakespeare's villain and the Tudor context
segments.summary: Hosts describe Shakespeare's hunchbacked Richard III and note the play likely flattered Queen Elizabeth, a Tudor descendant.

segments.title: Wars of the Roses begin
segments.summary: Overview of the York and Lancaster conflict over the English throne, the white and red roses, and Richard's father's role.

segments.title: Brutal rivalry and Edward IV's rise
segments.summary: Richard's father is killed and his head displayed with a paper crown; brother Edward defeats the Lancastrians at Towton and becomes king.

segments.title: George of Clarence and restored Lancaster rule
segments.summary: Brother George is executed for treason by drowning in wine; Henry VI is briefly restored in 1469 before the Yorks return in 1471.

segments.title: Richard becomes Lord Protector and then king
segments.summary: After Edward IV dies, Richard is named Lord Protector for the twelve-year-old Edward V, delays the coronation, and is crowned after rumors of illegitimacy; Hastings, Woodville and Grey are executed.

segments.title: The princes in the Tower and the Act of Parliament
segments.summary: The two princes are held in the Tower of London, and an Act of Parliament declares Richard legitimate heir in June 1483.

segments.title: Mid-episode break
segments.summary: Brief break in the episode.

segments.title: Disappearance of the princes and sources of the murder theory
segments.summary: The princes vanish from public view by 1483-1485; hosts discuss the Tyrrell theory, the later smothering account, and why motive alone is not strong evidence.

segments.title: Necklace evidence and why the history is unclear
segments.summary: A necklace tied to Edward V surfaces in a will linked to Tyrrell's sister-in-law; hosts explain lost records, Tudor destruction of documents, and the chronicles of Mancini and Croyland.

segments.title: Richard's reign, Buckingham rebellion and Bosworth
segments.summary: Debate over Richard's reign, including progressive measures, the Buckingham rebellion, personal tragedies, and his death at Bosworth Field in August 1485.

segments.title: Death wounds and burial
segments.summary: Richard's skull showed two fatal blows; his body was stripped, paraded and hastily buried at Greyfriars.

segments.title: Tudor succession and immediate smear campaign
segments.summary: Henry Tudor is crowned Henry VII on the battlefield; the Tudors begin a propaganda campaign against Richard.

segments.title: Rous and More's portrayals and physical deformity
segments.summary: John Rous and Thomas More portray Richard as monstrous; hosts argue the smear suggests he was not universally hated in life. Brief tangent on movies including The Goodbye Girl and Al Pacino's documentary.

segments.title: The Ricardians and the Richard III Society
segments.summary: The Richard III Society, founded in 1924, aims to rehabilitate Richard's reputation; members are called Ricardians and have chapters worldwide.

segments.title: The Daughter of Time
segments.summary: Josephine Tey's detective novel reimagines the princes' disappearance and casts doubt on Richard's guilt and historians' reliance on rumor.

segments.title: Philippa Langley's search begins
segments.summary: Inspired by Paul Murray Kendall's biography, Philippa Langley sets out to find Richard's body, narrowing it to downtown Leicester; an apartment site excavation finds no Greyfriars.

segments.title: Leicester car park excavation
segments.summary: Langley persuades the University of Leicester to survey and dig a car park; funding from the city council and the Richard III Society; excavation begins August 2012 and a skeleton is found within hours.

segments.title: Skeleton identified and press conferences
segments.summary: A September 2012 press conference describes an adult male with spinal curvature and head trauma; later DNA testing confirms the identity with about 99.9 percent certainty.

segments.title: The Lost King film and Langley's role
segments.summary: Hosts discuss Langley's contribution, the film The Lost King starring Sally Hawkins and Steve Coogan, and the criticism of the University of Leicester.

segments.title: Genealogical DNA matching and tangent
segments.summary: Researchers traced living descendants through a Canadian relative to match DNA; the hosts digress into tangents about Sally Hawkins and Paddington films.

segments.title: Reinterment and Langley's next project
segments.summary: Richard is reinterred at Leicester Cathedral with fanfare; the hosts note this doesn't resolve the princes' fate, and Langley turns to a project on the princes.

segments.title: Brief tangent on a music cease-and-desist
segments.summary: Hosts mention a cease-and-desist over Langley's princes claims and a music tangent about the Spin Doctors.

segments.title: Listener mail: Eagle Scout congratulations
segments.summary: A listener shares that her son became an Eagle Scout and invites the hosts to his court of honor; the hosts send congratulations and the email address.
